etermine, between 10^9 and 10^10, how many prime numbers there are by using the following criteria. Each less than 10 is a prime. If a number has two digits that are the same the number is not prime. If a number has three digits the first and last digits are the same the number is not prime. If a number has three digits the middle digit is the next lowest number ending in the first digit that is not equal to x the number is not prime. If a number has four digits or more the only digits other than the lowest are numbers ending in (i) the first lowest number that does not divide out the right end of the number, (ii) the lowest number that divides out the right end of the number, (iii) the next lowest number that does not divide out the right end of the number, (iv) the next lowest number that divides out the right end of the number, (v) the next lowest number that does not divide out the right end of the number, and the rest. This process continues for each perfect square number up to the right end of the number.

One of the challenges facing employment in modern society is the increasing automation and digitization of work, which requires workers to constantly update their skills to remain relevant in the job market. Additionally, the rapid pace of technological change can lead to job displacement for workers who lack the necessary skills to adapt. Workers also face issues such as high levels of stress and burnout due to the heavy workload and lack of work-life balance. Furthermore, unemployment and underemployment remain prevalent in many countries, especially among youth and marginalized groups.
